summary: 受禅代周、灭陈混一南北，以开皇制度奠定后世政制底盘，却因晚年废立与二世而亡留下争议的开国之主。
summary_en: Founding ruler who received Northern Zhou's abdication to establish the Sui and destroyed Chen to reunify north and south, laying the institutional foundation for later dynasties through the Kaihuang system, yet left controversy through the late-life change of heir and the dynasty's fall in the second generation.

bio_md:
# 隋文帝 · 主要事迹

杨坚以受禅方式代北周建隋，改元开皇。新朝初立，一面以政治手段清除北周宗室隐患、稳住局面，一面营迁大兴城，重定都城格局——开国的前几步，走得谨慎而彻底。

开皇七年，江陵后梁亡，南进之门洞开；开皇九年平陈，自东晋以来近三百年的南北分裂宣告结束，史称「混一戎夏」。次年江南反隋势力被平定，统一局面真正巩固。灭陈一役虽由诸将执行，战略决断皆出朝廷。

混一之外，开皇间三省六部成型、统一货币度量、检括户口，奠定此后数百年的政制底盘，后效极高。论文治的制度遗产，隋文帝在历代开国之主中位置很靠前。

晚年却是另一番走向：开皇二十年废太子勇、改立晋王广，储位之争自此埋下国祚风险。仁寿四年，文帝崩于仁寿宫，遗命与继位过程史有异说。其子[[sui-yang|隋炀帝]]即位，统一遗产与二世风险同时交接——废立争议与「二世而亡」的结局，压低了后世对这场开国之局的评价。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读：二者皆在长期分裂后完成混一，又皆在二代迅速陷入危局，是读统一帝国史绕不开的一对对照。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Jian replaced Northern Zhou and founded the Sui through an abdication, changing the era name to Kaihuang. With the new dynasty just established, he used political means to remove the lingering threat of the Northern Zhou royal house and steady the situation, while building and moving to Daxing and redesigning the capital's layout — the founding's first steps were taken with caution and thoroughness.

In Kaihuang 7, the Later Liang at Jiangling fell and the gate to the southern advance swung open; in Kaihuang 9 Chen was pacified, ending the nearly three-hundred-year division of north and south since the Eastern Jin — known in history as "the unification of the realm". The following year the anti-Sui forces in Jiangnan were suppressed, and the unified order was truly consolidated. Though the destruction of Chen was executed by his generals, every strategic decision came from the court.

Beyond unification, the Kaihuang era saw the Three Departments and Six Ministries take shape, currency and weights and measures unified, and households registered and checked — laying the institutional foundation of government for centuries to come, with exceptionally far-reaching aftereffects. In terms of institutional legacy, Emperor Wen ranks near the very front among the founding rulers of successive dynasties.

His later years took a different course: in Kaihuang 20 he deposed Crown Prince Yang Yong and installed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, in his place — and the struggle over the succession thereafter planted a risk to the dynasty's fortunes. In Renshou 4, Emperor Wen died at Renshou Palace; the historical record diverges on his dying orders and the succession process. His son

took the throne, and the legacy of unification was handed over together with the risk of a second-generation collapse — the controversy over the change of heir and the ending of "falling in the second generation" lowered later generations' appraisal of this founding. Read alongside
: both completed reunification after long division, and both quickly plunged into crisis in the second generation — an unavoidable pair for anyone reading the history of unified empires.
